name: Fermented-fish noodles
summary: Bún mắm is rice noodles in a fermented-fish broth that looks brown and still runs clear, with a sweet fish taste. It comes with roast pork and balut, and often shrimp, fish cake, and pork.
origin: A Mekong bowl adapted from a Cambodian soup made with prohok. In the west of the delta it is cooked with cá linh instead.
taste: The mắm turns the broth brown, but it stays clear, with a sweet fish taste.
howToEat: Eat it with roast pork and balut. Many bowls also add shrimp, fish cake, and pork.
The herbs are water-spinach tips, banana blossom, beansprouts, and fish mint.
where: Inside Chợ Châu Đốc, and at breakfast along the Hậu landing. Many Mekong towns serve it too.
seoDescription: Bún mắm in Châu Đốc is noodles in a clear brown fermented-fish broth with roast pork, balut, and river herbs, at the market and the landing.
